done.why: I couldn't work out the rules of the oddly-angled maze, and I never found a way to get water into the well bucket. That left the way up to the carousel's machinery closed.

about: A Colossal Cave-style cave of mislaid treasures. A Wizard's illusions give hints. The puzzles include a spinning carousel room, a riddle door, a well bucket and a maze tied to a baseball-diamond window.

moments.note: The Wizard gave a spoken map of the goals: pearls behind the riddle door, the rest past the carousel.
The gold ingot was an illusion and vanished when I tried to take it.
The Carousel Room scrambles directions, so exploring it was random.
Answering the riddle with 'well' opened the stone door and gave me the pearls.
The bucket needs water, but I found nothing to carry water in.
The oddly-angled maze gave inconsistent feedback and I couldn't find the sequence.

wished: A clearer way to tell which step in the maze was correct.
Somewhere to find a water container.
A way to stop the carousel from spinning.

lines.line: It is all south of the ravine, his look says, every treasure the Empire mislaid, and much good may it do you; the pearls nearest, behind a stone door that asks a question
lines.why: It set out the goal and the order of the puzzles.

lines.line: The floor, if you stand still on it a moment, is turning, slowly, and the eight passages go round with it
lines.why: It showed how the carousel puzzle works.

fun.why: Early progress was good: the Wizard's hints, the riddle and the pearls. I stalled on the water bucket and the maze.

engagement.why: The Wizard's hints gave me clear goals, but the randomized movement and the maze wore that down.

difficulty.why: The water-and-bucket step and the maze sequence were opaque, and I got no usable feedback on either.

interestingness.why: A varied cave with illusions, a carousel, a riddle and a baseball-themed maze.

prose.why: The prose was witty and the hints were embedded in the descriptions.
